# dsh-cookie-renew
Sliding renewal for the DSH web GUI's browser-session cookie.

DSH mints its `dsh-auth-*` cookie once, during the `?token=` exchange at
`GET /`, with an absolute e

xpiry (`connection.cookieMaxAgeDays`, default
30 days). Nothing refreshes it afterwards, so even a b

rowser that visits
every day has to reopen the tokenized startup URL once that absolute
lifetime ela

r that visits
every day has to reopen the tokenized startup URL once that absolute
lifetime elapses.

This host plugin keeps the session alive while the GUI is in use. It listens on
Connection's `connec

tion/request` waterfall — which wraps every authenticated
`/api` HTTP request after admission — and,

when the cookie's remaining
lifetime drops below a fraction of its total lifetime, re-runs DSH's ow

n token
exchange and attaches the fresh `Set-Cookie` to the live response.

- One runtime dependency (`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`), host-side only, Node >= 20.
- Installs from a

pinned tag:
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:edisoncks/dsh-cookie-renew#v1.0.0`
(see **Install*

*).
- Never reads the signing secret and never signs a cookie itself.
- Turns an absolute 30-day cre
dential into a renewable one (see **Caveats**).
## How it works

1. `connection/request` fires after `/api` admission and before the response
is written. The listene

r always calls `next()`, so API traffic is untouched.
2. The plugin locates the `dsh-auth-*` cookie

whose payload names the request's
normalized authority (`host:port` over HTTP, `https://host[:port]`

over
TLS). The payload is only a scheduling hint — its signature is not trusted
or checked. Candida

tes with a degenerate or already-elapsed payload are
skipped, so a stale or planted value cannot mas

k the real cookie.
3. When `remaining <= lifetime * renewBelowFraction` and the throttle has
elapsed

`ctx.connection.authorizeIndex()` runs the real exchange against a

process token is never persisted, and the cookie keeps working across
DSH restarts because the sign

ing secret lives in
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.
## Renewal cadence

Renewal is event-driven, not timed: it happens on the first `/api` request
after the threshold, whil

iven, not timed: it happens on the first `/api` request
after the threshold, while the page is open.
| Visits | Renewals with the default 30-day lifetime and `0.5` threshold |

| Daily | About every 15 days; expiry stays between 15 and 30 days out. |
| Every 20–29 days | Once

per visit. |
| One long idle tab | None while idle; the last mint's expiry still stands, so a tab id
le for the full lifetime still loses the session. |
`minIntervalMinutes` is a floor against mint storms, not the cadence.

The package is a DSH *bundle*. Its `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch: ./cordis.patch.yml`, a

nd that file mounts the plugin through
an `insert:` row. Selecting the bundle in the profile
(`dsh.p

rofile.bundles`) is what loads it **and** what makes it show up on the
sidebar **Plugins → Installed
plugins** page with a switch.

this package's one runtime dependency (`@deepseek

-ai/schemastery`) itself, so
no local `npm install` is involved.

## Caveats

- **Only while valid.** Admission rejects an expired cookie before the hook
runs, so a lapsed sessio

n still needs the printed `?token=` URL. This is a
keep-alive, not a re-login.
- **Only `/api` HTTP

requests.** WebSocket frames, static assets, and the index
page do not trigger a mint. Every page lo

ad issues API calls, so normal use is
covered.
- **Tied to the 0.2.1 line.** The hook and the two Co

nnection methods are
public, including the synthetic request/response shape, but the cookie
prefix,

the v1 payload shape, the authority spelling, the `303` status, and
the lowercase `set-cookie` key a

re internal. `engines.dsh` pins the verified
line, and an unknown payload version is logged once ins

tead of stopping
silently.
- **A stolen cookie becomes perpetually renewable.** Keep the GUI loopbac

k-only,
or bound exposure with `trustedHosts` and TLS.
- **Per authority.** Browsers ignore ports wh

en sending cookies; DSH binds this
cookie's name and payload to the request authority (`host:port` o

ver HTTP,
`https://host[:port]` over TLS) instead. Moving the GUI to another port
therefore needs a
fresh token exchange.
